decisions.statement: A folder matching any shape is right.
A folder's name never opens with the slug of the page above that folder.
A folder opening with that name is refused whatever shape the folder would match.
That refusal is answered before any shape is asked.
The name a folder is asked for is its page's own with that opening taken off.
The name a folder is asked for is never a name opening with the name the page above that folder has.
A folder is asked for no name where taking that opening off leaves nothing.
A shape says so rather than asking for a name that folder would be refused for.
A folder named for a part rather than for a page is asked for no such name.
A folder sitting under a part is named against the page above that part.
Every part between the folder and that page is looked through.
A folder named as an enabled shape's own name is a part of the page above that folder.
Those names are derived from the enabled shapes and the page types' plurals rather than named here.
Such a folder is judged of its own by the shape whose name that folder takes.
Passing such a folder over as a part loses no judgement.
A folder named by the one page in that folder is that page's own folder rather than a part.
Only a part is looked through when the page above a folder is looked for.
The refusal has each shape's reasons rather than ranking those shapes.
Every folder above a changed path is judged.
A folder the change reaches no path inside is judged.
A folder under a judged folder is judged only where the change reaches inside it.
The workspace root is judged by every change with a path.
A shape reads the folders under a folder as well as the files sitting in the folder.
No shape asks which files reach into the folder that shape judges.
An import the change adds or takes away widens what this check judges.
Which slugs are page types and which slugs name a file are read from the index the change leaves.
Which files sit in a folder is read as what git carries joined to the paths the change has.
What git carries is read at the commit the change is judged against.
A path another landing first carried after that commit sits in no folder here.
A folder already matching no shape that the change does not touch is named by nothing here.
Audit judges every folder.
A page this check has in hand is read from the index by that page's path.
A folder holding nothing but files some page's property names is no folder of its own.
The files such a folder holds are judged where the page declaring those files is judged.
A folder holding a subfolder is a folder of its own whatever else that folder holds.
That folder is passed over before any shape is asked.
Those segments are derived from the file properties rather than named in this check.
A folder looked through to find the page above is judged all the same.
Alan approved this check in the turn asking for it to judge.
An audit pays its reach once a run, so audit is given the longer ceiling.
A folder a change leaves holding no file and no folder is judged by no shape.
A file a generator writes shapes no folder, so no shape is shown that file.
Such a file beside a page leaves that page in the folder that page sat in.
A folder named its page's slug with every name above taken off is right as well.
A folder named a plural the page's own type gathers its pages under is right as well.

definition: the check refusing a folder matching none of the folder shapes
